newsitem.title: USA: Dell says UPS strike not hurting operations.
newsitem.headline: Dell says UPS strike not hurting operations.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp, the leading direct seller of computers, on Wednesday said the United Parcel Service strike was having no impact on its operations.
A company spokesman, T.R. Reid, told Reuters that Dell, in preparation for the work stoppage that began on Monday, began relying on its other shippers a week ago.
"For all intents and purposes, it's business as usual. It's required a change in the process, but in terms of any significant impact on our business, there hasn't been any," he said.
"Product is still getting outbound and still getting to customers in a timely fashion," Reid said.
UPS is one of several shippers that Dell uses routinely, but it is not the primary one, Reid said.

For "competitive reasons," he would not say how many items Dell ships daily, but the company's basic business model is to sell and ship its computers directly to the customer without going through retailers.

Reid would not comment directly when asked if the strike would affect revenues or earnings in the third quarter. But he said, "It has not had and we don't expect it will have any meaningful impact on our business. You can expand that, you can apply that to whatever you want."
